note: The main banks: Butterfield, RBC Royal Bank and CIBC Caribbean, three of the Cayman Islands' largest retail banks and card issuers (no Monetary Authority figures ranking card issuers were found). Butterfield Bank (Cayman)'s retail schedule of charges (last updated 1 December 2025, the one its site links as January 2026), read in full: its six personal cards in Cayman dollars, each with its primary card's annual fee (and the Miles Mastercard Platinum's $25 rewards fee, also yearly), its interest rate, its cash advance charge (2% with a $10 floor; 2.75% with a $5 floor on the AAdvantage Standard), a minimum payment of 3.5% of the balance with a $10 floor, the $45 late payment, $35 over-limit and $40 returned cheque fees. Its penalty rate for an account 60 days or more delinquent is the rate 'increased by 5% over current rate', read as five percentage points and written so (the six months' good standing before it reverts and the 60 days aren't modelled). The optional balance protection fee, the card replacement, auto-pay, rush card, limit increase and research fees, the AAdvantage Standard's $5,000 limit and the cash advance allowance aren't written. RBC Royal Bank's Cayman credit cards page (rendered 30 October 2026): its personal RBC Rewards Visa Platinum Black (for its Private Banking clients only, a condition the game doesn't check), RBC Rewards Visa Platinum, Visa Gold and Visa Classic International, in US dollars, each with its annual fee (none on the Black) and its 18% purchase and cash advance rates; its business and corporate cards aren't written, and the page states no other fee. CIBC Caribbean's Cayman schedule of charges isn't among those its site serves (30 October 2026), so its cards aren't written. This file kept RBC's Visa Classic International, read on 29 October 2026. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) also added CIBC Caribbean, one of the region's largest banks, whose Cayman schedule of charges for cards (effective may 2022, last updated july 2026) its site now serves (an earlier pass found it refused or not linked): read in full, its personal credit cards in US dollars (7), each with its annual fee for the primary card (none where the schedule gives 0.00 or Free; waived for the first year where the schedule says so), its yearly purchase rate, its cash advance rate and fee, its late payment, over-limit and returned cheque fees, the minimum payment where the schedule gives one, and its late payment rate as the penalty rate, as the earlier CIBC files do. Its business, corporate, commercial and Bizline cards aren't written, nor the replacement, statement, rush card, emergency payment and auto-payment charges, which a holder meets only by asking or by an auto-payment; the UWI cards are for the University of the West Indies' students, faculty and alumni, a condition the game doesn't check. It states no grace period or foreign transaction fee. Scotiabank was added in the same pass (30 October 2026), one of the islands' largest banks: its credit card interest rates and credit card fees pages, read in full: its Mastercard, Gold Mastercard and AAdvantage Mastercard in US dollars (18.99% to 23.99% a year, 18.99% on the Gold, written at the top with the bottom as the range's lowest), each with its annual membership fee, a minimum payment of 3%, at least $25, a $40 late payment fee, a $30 over-limit charge and a cash advance fee of 2.99%, at least $5, and the rate after a missed minimum payment on US dollar cards, up to 24.99%, written as the penalty rate; and The Platinum Card American Express in Cayman dollars (12.00%, CI$460 a year, a $33.55 late fee, a $35 over-limit charge, a 2.99% cash advance fee, at least $4, $25 for a returned cheque, a minimum payment of 3%, at least $20; the page's penalty sentence names only Jamaican and US dollar cards, so none is written for it); each with an interest-free period of at least 21 days on purchases paid in full, written as 21. The ScotiaLine cards (lines of credit) and the Platinum Card's US dollar side aren't written; the Mastercard returned cheque charge wasn't reached in the page's text, so none is written.
